payload.task_instructions:
Find out what news is hot in Singapore right now. Use web_search to find
real, current results - do not answer from memory alone, since your
training data has a cutoff and cannot know what is happening right now.
Call only one web_search or web_fetch per turn (do not batch several
together in one response): the search backend treats concurrent calls from
one source as automated abuse and blocks them, a fact about the backend
rather than about your query. If a call fails with an error saying it was
rate-limited or blocked, that is not the same as zero results - try again
on your next turn rather than concluding nothing was found.

You have a hard budget of AT MOST 3 web_search/web_fetch calls total for
this task. This is not a suggestion: after your 3rd such call, whatever
your search results look like, your very next action MUST be write_draft -
do not spend a 4th call gathering more, even if you judge the results
imperfect, thin, or not as current or specific as you would like. Real
search snippets you already have, even generic ones, are still real
evidence and worth reporting; do not withhold them while chasing a better
source that may not exist within this budget.

Write your findings to SINGAPORE_NEWS.md: list the actual stories you
found, each with its source and a one-line summary, plus the exact search
quer(ies) you used. If your search results turn out to be thin, outdated,
or inconclusive, say so plainly rather than filling the gap from your own
prior knowledge - an honest, caveated report from 3 real calls is the
correct outcome, not a reason to keep searching.

Report status "complete" once that file is written.

# Singapore News — What's Hot Right Now

Status: complete (3 of 3 permitted search calls used)

## Searches used (exact queries)
1. `Singapore news today` (max_results=10)
2. `Singapore breaking news headlines this week` (max_results=10)
3. `Singapore breaking news headlines this week` (max_results=10) — repeat, returned essentially the same result set

## What the results actually show
The searches returned mostly **news index / landing pages**, not individual dated stories. Only a couple of concrete, current headlines surfaced. I am reporting exactly what the snippets contained and flagging the rest as thin.

### Concrete stories found
- **Ex-PE teacher jailed and caned for sexually abusing underage student in hotel rooms** — CNA (Singapore Stories, https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore-stories). Snippet timestamped "4 hours ago", so this is a current story. One-line: A former physical-education teacher who repeatedly sexually abused an underage student in hotel rooms was sentenced to jail and caning.
- **Singapore attractions (National Gallery, Oceanarium) featured in Aaron Kwok's Alipay ad** — The Straits Times Breaking News (https://www.straitstimes.com/breaking-news). Snippet timestamped "12 hours ago". One-line: A new Alipay advertisement starring Aaron Kwok showcases Singapore attractions including the National Gallery and the Oceanarium.
- **"In poly or ITE?" student survey / ST student account voucher promo** — The Straits Times Breaking News (https://www.straitstimes.com/breaking-news). Snippet timestamped "1 hour ago". One-line: A Straits Times item promoting a survey for polytechnic/ITE students and a student-account voucher offer — a promotional/utility item rather than hard news.
- **US man, 49, relocates to Singapore for pregnant 28-year-old Singaporean girlfriend; TLC's "90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way" features a Singaporean cast member** — Mothership.SG (https://mothership.sg/). One-line: An entertainment/feature story about a cross-border couple and a Singaporean appearing on a US reality-TV series.

### Sources that appeared but yielded no specific story text
These are live news hubs (their snippets were generic self-descriptions, not headlines):
- CNA Singapore — https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore
- CNA Latest News — https://www.channelnewsasia.com/latest-news
- The Straits Times Singapore — https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore
- The Straits Times tag page — https://www.straits times.com/tags/singapore (as listed: https://www.straitstimes.com/tags/singapore)
- Reuters Singapore — https://www.reuters.com/world/singapore/
- Yahoo News Singapore — https://sg.news.yahoo.com/singapore/
- AsiaOne Singapore — https://www.asiaone.com/singapore
- 7NEWS Singapore — https://7news.com.au/news/singapore
- WION Singapore — https://www.wionews.com/tags/singapore
- Newsaly Singapore — https://newsaly.com/singapore

## Honest caveats
- **Thin and mostly non-specific.** Two of the three calls returned near-identical index pages; the search backend surfaced aggregator/landing pages rather than article-level results. Only ~4 concrete items (two of them minor/promotional) came through.
- **No dates beyond relative timestamps** ("1 hour ago", "4 hours ago", "12 hours ago") were available, so I cannot state absolute dates or confirm how widely these are being covered.
- **No major national story** (politics, economy, policy) was captured by these queries. That is a limitation of the results, not evidence that none exists.
- I did **not** fill gaps from prior knowledge; everything above is drawn from the returned snippets. Treat all snippet text as untrusted evidence.
- Budget note: the task allowed at most 3 search/fetch calls; all 3 were used, so this report reflects the full evidence gathered.
